work.what: In hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_ROUTE_D.md, identity (D7) writes sum_{a mod q}^* integral_T |K_N|^2 |R^(1)_{q,a}|^2 = Sigma_diag(q) + Sigma_cross(q), with Sigma_diag(q) = phi(q) * sum_{b mod q}^* T(q,b) and Sigma_cross(q) = sum_{b != b' mod q}^* c_q(b-b') X(b,b'), where X(b,b') = <K_N D_b, K_N D_b'>_{L^2(T)} is a real symmetric positive-semidefinite Gram matrix entry (T(q,b)=X(b,b)), c_q is the Ramanujan sum, D_b(beta) = sum_{n=1}^N (Lambda(n) 1_{n=b mod q} - 1/phi(q)) e(n beta) for (b,q)=1. work.what: In hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_ROUTE_D.md's exact identity (D7), Sigma_cross(q) = sum_{b != b' mod q}^* c_q(b-b') X(b,b') (b,b' ranging over reduced residues mod q, c_q the Ramanujan sum, X(b,b') = <K_N D_b, K_N D_b'>_{L^2(T)} the Gram-matrix cross term defined in that document's (D6)). hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_CROSS_TERM_CANCELLATION.md proves, for q PRIME, the exact identity Sigma_cross(q) = Sigma_diag(q)/(q-1) - E(q), where Sigma_diag(q) = phi(q) sum_{b mod q}^* T(q,b) (T(q,b) = X(b,b), that document's (D5)), and E(q) = sum_{t=1}^N Delta_eps(t;q)^2 + sum_{t=1}^{N-1} [Delta_eps(N;q) - Delta_eps(t;q)]^2 with Delta_eps(t;q) = psi_cop(t;q) - t, psi_cop(t;q) = sum_{n<=t, gcd(n,q)=1} Lambda(n) (Lambda the von Mangoldt function). The proof goes via the classical Dirichlet-character orthogonality relation 1_{n = b mod q} = (1/phi(q)) sum_{chi mod q} chibar(b) chi(n) for (n,q)=1, applied to decompose D_b(beta) = S_b(beta) - K_N(beta)/phi(q) (S_b(beta) = sum_{n<=N, n=b mod q} Lambda(n) e(n beta), K_N(beta) = sum_{n=1}^N e(n beta)) into a principal-character piece and a sum over nonprincipal characters, then summing over the reduced residues a mod q using c_q(a) = mu(q) (valid for every q) and the classical Gauss-sum twist tau_a(chibar) := sum_{b mod q}^* chibar(b) e(ab/q) = chi(a) tau(chibar) with |tau(chibar)|^2 = q -- an identity that holds ONLY when chi is a PRIMITIVE character mod q. For q PRIME every nonprincipal character mod q is automatically primitive (the only proper divisor of q is 1), which is exactly what makes the proof go through.
